# Borrowing from the public - Federal securities (in millions)
# From 2020 bulletin (element 176) and 2024 bulletin (element 173)

    2016: 1051824,  # from 2020 bulletin element 176
    2017: 498301,   # from 2020 bulletin element 176
    2018: 1084458,  # from 2020 bulletin element 176
    2019: 1051606,  # from 2020 bulletin element 176

    2022: 1969817,  # from 2024 bulletin element 173
    2023: 1982672,  # from 2024 bulletin element 173
    2024: 1959809,  # from 2024 bulletin element 173
}

print("Borrowings from the public - Federal securities (millions):")
for year, value in borrowings.items():
    print(f"FY{year}: {value:,}")

# Get values in order
values = [borrowings[2016], borrowings[2017], borrowings[2018], borrowings[2019], 
          borrowings[2020], borrowings[2021], borrowings[2022], borrowings[2023], borrowings[2024]]

print("\nOriginal values:", values)

# Take natural log
logs = [math.log(v) for v in values]
print("\nNatural logs:", logs)

# 20% trimmed mean: trim 20% from each end
# 20% of 9 = 1.8, so trim 1 from each end (or 2 from total = 20%)
# Actually 1/9 ≈ 11.1%, 2/9 ≈ 22.2% - let's trim 1 from each end to be closest to 20%
n = len(logs)
trim_count = 1  # trim 1 from each end (total 2 trimmed = 22.2% - closest to 20%)

trimmed = sorted(logs)[trim_count:-trim_count]
print(f"\nSorted logs: {sorted(logs)}")
print(f"Trimmed values (removing {trim_count} from each end): {trimmed}")

# Calculate mean of trimmed values
trimmed_mean = sum(trimmed) / len(trimmed)
print(f"\n20% trimmed mean of logs: {trimmed_mean}")
print(f"Rounded to 3 decimal places: {round(trimmed_mean, 3)}")

arguments.command:
python3 << 'EOF'
import math

# Verify calculation
# Borrowing from the public - Federal securities (in millions)
borrowings = {
    2016: 1051824,
    2017: 498301,
    2018: 1084458,
    2019: 1051606,
    2020: 4216280,
    2021: 1267947,
    2022: 1969817,
    2023: 1982672,
    2024: 1959809,
}

# Get values in order
values = [borrowings[2016], borrowings[2017], borrowings[2018], borrowings[2019], 
          borrowings[2020], borrowings[2021], borrowings[2022], borrowings[2023], borrowings[2024]]

# Take natural log
logs = [math.log(v) for v in values]

# Sort and trim 1 from each end (for 20% trimmed mean with 9 values)
sorted_logs = sorted(logs)
trimmed = sorted_logs[1:-1]  # Remove smallest 1 and largest 1

# Calculate mean
trimmed_mean = sum(trimmed) / len(trimmed)
print(f"Sorted logs: {[round(x, 6) for x in sorted_logs]}")
print(f"Trimmed (1 from each end): {[round(x, 6) for x in trimmed]}")
print(f"Count: {len(trimmed)}")
print(f"20% trimmed mean (after taking ln): {trimmed_mean:.6f}")
print(f"Rounded to 3 decimal places: {round(trimmed_mean, 3)}")
EOF
